how: Shanghai Cricket Club runs a two-division league and welcomes casual players, playing at the Shanghai Community Sports Club in Pudong.
venue: Shanghai Cricket Club (Shanghai Community Sports Club ground)

how: Shanghai Rugby Football Club trains weekly at Wellington College (Tue) and Harrow International School (Sat) and welcomes complete newcomers; Dolphins Rugby also runs touch and contact sessions at Luwan Stadium.
Shanghai Ultimate Players Association plays pick-up games on Monday nights at Jing'an Workers' Stadium and Saturday mornings at Shanghai Community Sports Club for about RMB 50 per session.
Shanghai GAA (founded 2002) trains Tuesday evenings at Luwan Stadium; training is free to try and absolute beginners are welcome.
Dragon Fencing Center teaches adult beginners with an annual membership that includes a weekly group lesson (2015 SmartShanghai profile; current status unconfirmed).
Shanghai Hockey Club runs adult ice hockey with a skate assessment used for team placement.
All Star Skating Club under the Mercedes-Benz Arena is among Shanghai's better rinks, and SmartShanghai lists a dozen-plus rinks citywide including Hongqiao Ice Sports Center.

Shanghai has a few curling sites (Putuo Ice Sports Center converted rinks into five sheets for the 2026 national championships; Dream World Qingpu has a rink for hockey and curling), but public drop-in curling was not confirmed.
BANANA+ in The Lightbox is a large Jing'an bouldering gym with beginner-friendly problems; Pongo and Beta Boulders are other dedicated bouldering gyms.
Acme Climbing at 189 Plaza and Magirock offer top-rope and lead walls with harness and shoe rental and basic instruction.
Shanghai Westend Equestrian Club on Changxing Island offers English-style group and private lessons with a trial class; roughly an hour's drive from downtown.
Shanghaied Dragons is an amateur expat dragon boat team that accepts paddlers of any ability and trains beginners with weeknight practices.
Latin Soul Dance Studio teaches salsa (On1, On2, rueda) and bachata classes Monday to Friday evenings for all levels; ByC! and Phoenix studios also teach bachata.
Zmack Improv has performed in English since 2009 and runs Zmack Comedy School improv classes for adults.
SpicyComedy in Xintiandi runs English stand-up showcases most nights, sometimes with open-mic formats.
The Pottery Workshop teaches wheel throwing to adults in English or Chinese, seven days a week.
Meet Pottery and Taoni Xuanxiao offer drop-in DIY hand-building and wheel sessions for RMB 120-158 including firing.
IdleBeats Print Club in Xuhui runs two-hour beginner screen-printing workshops in English and Chinese plus open-studio blocks.
Lao Feng Xiang hosted a one-off expat silver pendant design-and-polish workshop at its Yuyuan Garden flagship in 2026; regular classes were not confirmed.
venue: Lao Feng Xiang flagship, Yuyuan Garden Malls

how: Capoeira Mandinga Shanghai lists classes (kids confirmed); an older expat thread describes adult beginner sessions near Zhongshan Park.
Mingwu martial arts school lists taekwondo alongside taiji, sanda and Thai boxing in a SmartShanghai martial arts listing.
ICONX operates one of Shanghai's first indoor skateparks at Jing'an Sports Center, and SMP Skatepark in Yangpu is billed as China's biggest; Linkong Skateboard Park in Changning is an outdoor park.
Smile Snow in Changning and SHEERCOOL have ski simulators; L+SNOW in Lin-gang (Pudong) is a very large year-round indoor snow resort, roughly 55 km from the centre.
No bobsleigh or skeleton track exists in the Shanghai region; the nearest is the Yanqing track near Beijing, about 1,100 km away.
No ski jumping hill exists near Shanghai; hills are in northern China such as Zhangjiakou (Chongli) near Beijing, about 1,100 km away.
Buzkashi is a Central Asian horseback game and is not played in the Shanghai area; the nearest traditions are in Xinjiang, thousands of km away.
Camel racing needs camels and desert terrain; nothing comparable exists near Shanghai (nearest in Inner Mongolia/Xinjiang, thousands of km away).

how: Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling is an annual event in Gloucestershire, England, with no equivalent in the Shanghai region.
Elephant polo requires working elephants, which are not kept in the Shanghai region; it is played in Thailand, Nepal and India (about 5-hour flights).
The Yangtze estuary coast near Shanghai is muddy and shallow with no reliable surf; the nearest surf spots are in Hainan (for example Riyue Bay), around a 3-hour flight.
Shanghai Hash House Harriers hold weekly Sunday trail walk/run events at rotating locations, and RunnersHai runs free social runs at West Bund; true trail terrain is limited by the flat delta.

Sheshan National Forest Park offers hill trails within the city, while longer hikes require trips to hills in neighbouring Zhejiang or Jiangsu, such as the guided Changzhou trips sold to Shanghai expats.
Shanghai has a handful of designated park camping areas and a guided camping trip trade for expats, though most multi-night camping happens in neighbouring provinces.
venue: Guided camping and hiking trips (Hello China Trip)

how: New Jiangwan City Culture and Sports Park in Yangpu has a professionally managed water sports centre for paddleboarding and kayaking, with Direction Kayak ASSN training at Nianfeng Park.
venue: New Jiangwan City Culture and Sports Park water sports centre

how: Danba Art Dock in Putuo offers sunset paddleboard yoga and paddle polo, and Tingdong Kayaking Club teaches beginner paddleboarding.
Shanghai Sailing Club on Dishui Lake runs sailing courses from beginner to advanced and rents boats; the lake is about 55 km from the centre.
Shanghai Sailing Club at Dishui Lake rents dinghies and offers dinghy courses; the lake is about 55 km from the centre.
Shanghai Sailing Club rents Fareast keelboats on Dishui Lake, and Haishang Fanyou Sailing and Yacht Club operates nearby.
Big Blue Scuba Diving International runs 400 RMB discovery dives in a pool in Qibao and PADI courses with open-water dives at Qiandao Lake.
Studio Insight offers one-on-one and group guitar lessons with local and expat teachers, with a trial class listed at RMB 58.
Studio Insight offers one-on-one and group piano lessons with local and expat teachers.
Gate Music in Changning is an Ableton-certified training centre teaching music production with bilingual materials and international instructors.
Gate Music and Studio Insight teach DJing with international instructors; C-Space in Jing'an is another DJ school.
InkMoon Workshop on Fumin Lu runs small-group (max six) one-off and long-term calligraphy classes for RMB 280 per person.
Salon de Verve on Huashan Lu runs three-hour oil painting classes by appointment with canvas, paints and instructor included.
Make in China on Jiashan Lu runs three-hour weaving, macrame, block printing, embroidery and crochet workshops; Shanghai Mass Art Museum also has a 12-session embroidery course for foreigners.
Make in China runs three-hour weaving and macrame workshops at about RMB 400 per person.
Make in China lists crochet among its three-hour craft workshops; dedicated knitting groups were not confirmed.
Shanghai Museum of Glass runs hands-on glassmaking workshops priced RMB 98-380; whether full hot glassblowing is included was not confirmed.
InLove Sports Club in Huangpu has two indoor pickleball courts, and Rocker Park at Bailian Xijiao in Changning converts to four courts.
PadelX operates two padel courts at Bailian Xijiao Shopping Center in Changning, open 7am to midnight.
Shanghai Voices International Choir has drawn members from over 20 countries since 2000, and the Shanghai Citizen Art Night School runs singing classes for expats.
Dance Flow Studio near iAPM and Dance Box offer adult ballet and contemporary classes.
La Luna in Minhang is a studio specialising in pole dancing, with yoga and contemporary classes.
Luyuan Fishing Leisure Center in Pudong has man-made ponds for day-ticket carp fishing, and Fishing Bay Ecological Garden in Xinchang has fishing ponds.
Luyuan Fishing Leisure Center in Pudong has man-made ponds for bamboo-rod day-ticket carp fishing (2017 SmartShanghai article).

Sheshan Observatory's historic 40-cm telescope has been partially opened to booked public visits since 2023, and the Shanghai Astronomy Museum in Lin-gang offers night views through a one-metre telescope; no amateur club was found.
